body.input: Which cloud and data centre companies expanded to Denmark in 2026?

response.content:
## Cloud and Data Centre Companies That Expanded to Denmark in 2026

Several cloud and data centre companies made notable expansions into or within Denmark during 2026:

### 1. **Microsoft**
Microsoft launched its **"Denmark East" cloud region** in 2026, described as the company's largest single investment in its 36-year history in Denmark. The new region includes data centres across the municipalities of **Esbjerg and Varde** in Western Denmark, as well as facilities in the capital area and Zealand. The investment was characterised as a "multi-billion dollar" commitment. All energy consumption is matched with 100% carbon-free energy through long-term power purchase agreements.

### 2. **CoreWeave**
CoreWeave brought its **first deployment in Denmark** online in 2026, housed at atNorth's **DEN01 data centre in Copenhagen**. The facility uses Nvidia Blackwell systems and high-speed networking technology to support AI workloads. This expanded CoreWeave's European infrastructure footprint to nine data centres across five geographies.

### 3. **Interxion (Digital Realty)**
Interxion, a Digital Realty company, expanded its Copenhagen campus with the construction of **CPH3**, its third data centre in Denmark. Located in Ballerup on the outskirts of Copenhagen, the facility is designed to deliver nearly 7,000 square metres of equipped space and over 14 MW of customer capacity when fully built out.

### 4. **Dansk Data Center 1 (DDC1) — CIP, Thylander & PensionDanmark**
Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), Thylander, and PensionDanmark started construction on **DDC1** at the **Port of Esbjerg**. DDC1 is designed as an energy-integrated data centre focused on energy efficiency, security of supply, and integration into the local energy system, serving as a pilot for future Danish data centres.

### 5. **Thylander Data Centers**
Danish real estate firm Thylander announced plans to develop a new **AI-ready co-location data centre** in Denmark with potential to expand to a 200 MW grid connection, targeting businesses that need local data storage and processing with advanced GPU infrastructure.

### Other notable existing/expanding players
Market reports identify **Apple, Meta, Google, STACK Infrastructure, GlobalConnect, Bulk Infrastructure, AtlasEdge, Cibicom, Telia, and NNIT** as key data centre investors active in Denmark during this period, with Apple and Meta specifically noted as expanding their operations in the country.

context.content: # CIP and Thylander start construction of energy-integrated data centre in Denmark backed by PensionDanmark. The project is backed by Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), Thylander, Plexar, and PensionDanmark.*. The new project aims to showcase how data centres can be developed in close collaboration with the local energy system, working not just as a consumer of electricity, but as an integral part of the broader energy infrastructure. DDC1 will be one of the largest data centres in Denmark and is owned by PensionDanmark, the Thylander Group, and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), through its CI Microgrid Electrification Fund. DDC1 is a pilot project designed to serve as a framework for the Danish data centres of the future, where digital infrastructure is developed in closer collaboration with the energy system and with a focus on local value creation and resource utilisation. Dansk Data Center 1 (DDC1) is a Danish-owned data centre being built at the Port of Esbjerg in Denmark and developed with a focus on energy efficiency, security of supply, and integration into the energy system.

context.content: Thylander, a 40-year-old Copenhagen-based private equity real estate firm, has plans to develop a new AI-ready data center in several phases (with potential to expand to a 200 MW grid connection) in Denmark and lease rack space, networking, power, and cooling to businesses that require bleeding-edge graphics processing units (GPUs) and other hardware for AI workloads. Beginning in 2024, Thylander recognized an opportunity to develop and operate Danish co-location data centers: Some businesses require their data to be stored and processed locally, and many want to raise the standards for energy optimization in data centers. “Looking at data sovereignty and thinking about who actually owns data centers was the starting point to do something Danish for Danish companies—as well as for externals who think the Danish markets are valuable,” says Anders Mathiesen, chief executive of Thylander Data Centers. The United States hosts more data centres than any other country by far, currently about 4,000. They draw down 5 percent of the nation’s electricity. Yet the US recovers very little heat because it has nowhere to go.

“We should be building data centres where their heat can be used, not just where land is cheapest,” said Jan Rosenow, professor of energy and climate policy at the University of Oxford.

Scandinavia has been leading the way on capturing waste heat, Rosenow said. “Meta’s data centre in Odense in Denmark recovers around 100 GWh a year, enough for 6,900 homes. And Stockholm in Sweden has been feeding data centre heat into its network since 2014.” [...] Live
